newsitem.title: USA: Russia wins $600 mln World Bank loan - Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Russia wins $600 mln World Bank loan - Chubais.

text.p: Russia and the World Bank have signed a protocol on a new structural adjustment loan and Russia expects to receive the credit by June, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.

Chubais told a news conference that the World Bank would also increase an existing $500 million social policy loan to $800 million. He said preparatory work on a second loan to restructure the coal sector would not be dependent on the results of the first loan, which has already been released.

"In real terms it means that, by the end of the first half, Russia will receive more than half a billion dollars from the World Bank," he said. "This is a radical change in the relationships between Russia and the World Bank."
World Bank vice president Johannes Linn told reporters that negotiations on the $600 million loan had been completed on Tuesday.
"Following the completion of some outstanding policy actions, we will look for board approval of this operation on June 5," he said.
World Bank lending to Russia is currently being used for budget support -- including paying wage arrears -- and to support broad economic policies.
Officials there expect more targeted loans in the future, helping reconstruct specific parts of the Russian infrastructure or guarantee financing for major projects such as pipelines.
World Bank President James Wolfensohn has said the institution might be in a position to lend Russia some $6 billion over the next two years.
